intended_object: The standard correspondence that sends a monomorphism [n] → [m] in the simplex category Δ (an injective order-preserving map) to the matching morphism [n]ₛ → [m]ₛ of the semi-simplex category Δ_inj, whose morphisms are order embeddings. In other words, it lifts a mono along the inclusion functor Δ_inj → Δ. Inferred from the docstring and from the lemma `toSimplexCategory_map_homOfMono`.
explanation:
The definition is correct. Its input is a morphism `f : ⦋n.len⦌ ⟶ ⦋m.len⦌` in `SimplexCategory` that is a mono. By `SimplexCategory.mono_iff_injective`, its underlying order hom is injective. A monotone injective map out of a linear order is strictly monotone, so `OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono` turns it into an order embedding `Fin (n.len+1) ↪o Fin (m.len+1)`. That is exactly the data of a morphism in `SemiSimplexCategory`, which `homEquiv.symm` packages as one.

The next lemma, `toSimplexCategory_map_homOfMono`, shows that the result maps back to `f` under the inclusion functor. So `homOfMono` is the expected preimage of a mono under the faithful functor `toSimplexCategory`.

The definition is mostly an API constructor, but it does encode a real mathematical fact: the morphisms of the semi-simplex category are exactly the monomorphisms of Δ. Nothing here can be generalised, since the setting is fixed by the semi-simplex category itself. I found no separate Mathlib declaration for this lift.
